geography: Du Sable homestead compound on the north bank of the Chicago River
source_locator: PDF pp. 5-6; May 7, 1800 deed inventory
interpretation: A parcel-level compound count, not a count for the Chicago settlement. The nomination enumerates only nine functions including the main house, so the tenth building's function remains unidentified.

geography: Chicago River mouth civilian settlement, excluding the new federal fort
source_locator: Vol. I, printed p. 72; Whistler-arrival passage
interpretation: Juliette Kinzie's retrospective account reports four traders' huts: Le Mai, Ouilmette, Pettell, and a possible Burnett house. The count is stronger than the identity of the fourth occupant.

geography: Chicago settlement outside Fort Dearborn
source_locator: Vol. I, printed p. 84; 'After the Massacre'
interpretation: Five civilian houses: Kinzie, Ouilmette, Burns, Lee near the fort, and the Lee-farm house. Excludes Fort Dearborn and its attached agency house and therefore must not be added to later municipal-stock series without a geography crosswalk.

geography: Chicago Indian Agency settlement as described by visitor John H. Fonda; boundary not municipal
source_locator: Vol. I, printed pp. 100-101; Fonda recollection
interpretation: Fonda said Chicago contained about fourteen houses. 'About' and the absence of a surveyed boundary make this a rounded visitor estimate, not a parcel census.

geography: Peoria County assessment roll entries associated with Chicago and outlying North/South Branch residents
source_locator: Vol. I, printed pp. 100-101; Bogardus assessment roll
interpretation: A fiscal denominator, not a building count. Several taxpayers lived miles up the branches and at least one had quarters with another taxpayer; do not use fourteen taxpayers as fourteen independent structures.

geography: River-mouth settlement, Hardscrabble, and the Clybourne North Branch cabins; Fort Dearborn excluded
source_locator: Vol. I, printed pp. 102-103 plus Clybourne-family passage
interpretation: Derived non-fort range: Beaubien cabin and warehouse (2), double-log agency house (1), blacksmith shop (1), store cabin (1), Hardscrabble cabins (5-6), and two Clybourne cabins (2). Includes commercial/storage structures as well as houses and may omit unremembered structures.

geography: Chicago town, principally north and south sides below the forks
source_locator: Vol. I, 1833 growth narrative
interpretation: Andreas says nearly 150 frame buildings were built in spring and summer 1833. This is construction flow, not year-end stock; 150 is retained as the stated approximate ceiling.

geography: Chicago town, mostly Canal Section 9
source_locator: Vol. I, 1834 boom narrative
interpretation: Andreas says over 150 houses, stores, and shanties were put up in spring and early summer. This is a lower bound on construction flow, not a stock count.

geography: City of Chicago corporate limits at the 1837 incorporation-era census
source_locator: Vol. I, city census table immediately after population total 4,170
interpretation: The source's OCR reads 'dwellingo' but the printed category is dwellings. This residential count excludes or overlaps nonresidential categories in undocumented ways; do not sum mechanically with taverns, churches, or stores.

geography: City of Chicago corporate limits at the 1837 incorporation-era census
source_locator: Vol. I, city census table immediately after population total 4,170
interpretation: Contemporaneous category count. Category boundaries and mixed-use treatment are not documented, so this is not safely additive to the dwelling count.

geography: City of Chicago corporate limits at the 1837 incorporation-era census
source_locator: Vol. I, city census table immediately after population total 4,170
interpretation: Contemporaneous category count. Taverns may also have contained dwellings; treat it as a use-category statistic rather than an additional mutually exclusive stock count.

geography: City of Chicago corporate limits at the 1837 incorporation-era census
source_locator: Vol. I, city census table immediately after population total 4,170
interpretation: Contemporaneous category count. The named-structure CSV currently has fewer records because its inclusion standard requires an identifiable building, while this is an aggregate census category.

geography: Chicago area; Encyclopedia entry does not equate this wording to 1840 corporate limits
source_locator: Opening historical paragraph
interpretation: The Encyclopedia says the Chicago area had fewer than 1,000 structures in 1840. This is a rounded regional-area ceiling and is not directly comparable with the 1837 corporate-limit dwelling count.

geography: Chicago; historical boundary/coverage not restated by Hoyt
interpretation: Hoyt reports 600 new buildings erected in 1844. This is annual construction flow. His footnote chain should be traced before treating it as permit-grade data.

geography: Chicago; historical boundary/coverage not restated by Hoyt
interpretation: Hoyt reports 871 new buildings erected in 1845. This is annual construction flow, not stock. A newspaper summary of the 1844 directory appears to associate 871 with its reporting year, so the original directory/newspaper chronology still requires reconciliation.

geography: Chicago area; Encyclopedia entry does not equate this wording to corporate limits
source_locator: Opening historical paragraph
interpretation: The Encyclopedia says the area's structure count passed 10,000 around 1854. Encoded as a strict lower bound and not an exact annual observation.

geography: Great Chicago Fire burned district across the West, South, and North divisions
source_locator: Vol. II, Great Fire chapter, first 'Area of Burned District' estimate
interpretation: A preliminary estimate reproduced by Andreas: South 3,000, North 10,000, with the total stated as 13,500 after including the West. It is an alternative estimate, not additive to later fire-loss rows.

geography: Great Chicago Fire burned district across the West, South, and North divisions
source_locator: Vol. II, later Chicago Relief and Aid Society report
interpretation: The division figures sum to 17,450 destroyed buildings (500 West, 3,650 South, 13,300 North), while the report rounds the burned area's contents to 18,000 buildings. The range preserves that internal rounding; do not add either endpoint to another estimate.

geography: Great Chicago Fire burned district
source_locator: Vol. II, letter to Rufus Blanchard dated April 24, 1883
interpretation: Retrospective compilation described by its author as based on nearly reliable data. This is an alternate historical estimate, not an additional loss category.

geography: Great Chicago Fire burned district, 3.5 square miles in the heart of the city
source_locator: Full entry
interpretation: Modern synthesis states that more than 18,000 structures were leveled. Encoded as a strict lower bound; it corroborates the high contemporary estimate but does not resolve building-versus-structure terminology.
